newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ericsson sees Asian expansion continuing.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson sees Asian expansion continuing.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Thursday that growth of mobile phone systems in Asia continued and could speed up.
"We expect it to continue, as it has done so far, and we think it could even accelerate," said Kurt Hellstrom, head of Ericsson's Mobile Systems division in an interview with Reuters.

"Nothing indicates that it would fall, as costs drop across the board on networks, telephones and subscriber fees," he said, adding that a mobile system's infrastructure was cheaper than that of a fixed network.
Hellstrom said that growth was also strong in developed markets, such as Japan, where the number of mobile phone subscribers rose by 10 million last year.
"In Japan, operators think they will reach a penetration of 50 percent in the year 2000," he added.
In China, Ericsson hopes private ownership in telecoms networks -- currently under discussion -- will be allowed.

"We hope so," Hellstrom said. "There is, however, a limit to what you can handle growthwise. We must get knowledgeable local partners and that is difficult...there has always been a lack of knowledgeable people in the business," he said.
India and Latin America also had large potential, he said.
"Penetration in Asia is just in its infancy," Hellstrom said. "We have just scratched the surface.
"India has the prerequisites to become a gigantic market and also in Latin America there is a lot to do. The need is almost inexhaustible."
Hellstrom does not see the development of satellite telephones as a direct threat to Ericsson.
"I do not for example think that Europe will be affected by satellite telephones. An existing complete GSM system already exists here,"
GSM, global system for mobile communications, is the mobile telephony standard used in Europe and many other parts of the world.
